question: Difference between Hoya 58CIR or Hoya HMC ? Trying to decide between the regular Hoya Circular Polaraizing Filter or the HMC. Does the more expensive HMC give that much better results to justify the price?
gold_answer: Yes it does.  I would never consider using a non-multi-coated filter on a digital camera.  The reason is simple.  The sensor has a flat glass protecting it (called a low-pass filter - LPF).  Some light will bounce off the LPF and head out the lens.  Since lens elements are multi-coated and curved, very little light will reflect back to the sensor.  But since the front filter IS flat, you can get a lot of light bouncing back.  If you use a non-coated, or single-coated filter, you get a lot of light reflected back into the sensor.  This shows up as a loss of contrast (veiling flair) or as ghosts and hot spots.  Multi-coated filters are designed to reduce this effect, but cannot eliminate it.  This is a real problem when you shoot into a light source.When shooing into a light, ANY filter will degrade the image.  Multi-coated filters are much better, though.
